_note: THE UNIT PLANE. An editor that offers rem and px must answer one question honestly: what happens to the NUMBER when the unit changes. Converting (16px -> 1rem) keeps the rendered size and changes how the author says it; reinterpreting (16px -> 16rem) makes a headline sixteen times larger while claiming to have changed nothing. These cases pin CONVERT, plus the two behaviours a unit switch must never have: destroying a value it cannot parse, and losing precision when switched twice.

convert.name: px to rem divides by the root
a real headline size converts to a readable decimal
rem to px multiplies by the root
already in the target unit is a relabel, never a re-scale
em is the element's own size, so the editor reads it against the root as rem
a bare number is px by CSS's own reading
a negative offset converts like any other length
a percentage is of its container and has no rem equivalent, so it passes through
an expression the author wrote deliberately is never mangled

unitOf.name: px is read from the value
rem is read from the value
em reads as rem, the unit the editor offers
a bare number reports the DEFAULT rather than pretending to know
an unparsable value reports the default
a percentage is not a switchable unit, so the default stands
